beta_note: Each case is shown with the passage we matched; read it before you cite the case. Measured: 81% of shown cases support the sentence, 1 in 73 did not (details on /measurements).
court_note: No court chosen: Supreme Court cases come first. Choose your court to see which cases bind it.
message: This reads as a question. Paste the rule itself, as a sentence, and we will look for cases that state it.
about: How we build this list: we search the sentences in which federal appellate courts and the Supreme Court cite a case, and the cases' own text. A judgment model then reads the opinion of the court in each of the top 10 candidates. We show a case only when the model finds a passage in it that states your sentence, at confidence 0.8 or higher. We leave out cases that a later court overruled or reversed.

measured.readers: two blind model readers per item, a third on the one disagreement
measured.source: citation-bench PROGRESS.md Phase 8, round 3, set C

example: A complaint must contain sufficient factual matter, accepted as true, to state a claim to relief that is plausible on its face.
